newsitem.title: USA: N.J. casino agency asks for Trump probe.
newsitem.headline: N.J. casino agency asks for Trump probe.

text.p: New Jersey's Casino Reinvestment Development Authority asked the state Attorney General on Tuesday to investigate allegations of anti-competitiveness by Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc.
James Kennedy, the agency's executive director, said he was asking for the probe in response to a lawsuit filed against the agency last month by Trump Hotels.

That lawsuit seeks to block a $330 million tunnel project in Atlantic City the agency is helping to finance over the objections of developer Donald Trump. Trump argued the project unfairly benefits a rival developer, Steve Wynn, by providing access to his proposed Mirage Resorts Inc hotel in the marina district.
But Kennedy, in a letter to the director of the Attorney General's Division of Gaming Enforcement, said Trump's actions to block the tunnel warranted an investigation.

"Where the exercise of free speech becomes actions which are only a guise for anticompetitive activities by a casino licensee, the DGE and the Casino Control Commmission should take appropriate action," Kennedy said.
Officials at Trump Hotels were not immediately available for comment.

Kennedy specifically asked the gaming enforcement division to investigate whether Trump Hotels had funded litigation to stop public works projects because they would benefit casino properties owned by Trump rivals or took other actions that would have the same effect.
Kennedy said the agency's mission is to encourage development that by definition would benefit specific casinos, and said Trump Hotels had been the beneficiary of such projects in the past.
